facts.claim: Domènech i Montaner built the Palau from 1905 to 1908 as headquarters of Orfeó Català in Sant Pere.
facts.excerpt: lau de la Música Catalana was built between 1905 and 1908 by Lluís Domènech i Montaner as the headquarters of the Orfeó Català, funded through public subscription. It stands in the Sant Pere quarter, one of Barcelona’s most characterful areas. UNESCO World Heritage Site The Palau de la Música Catalana is an architectural jewel of Catalan modernism and the only concert hall to have been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site (4 December 1997). Today, it is a key venue in Catalonia’s musical and cultural life, as well as a deeply symbolic landmark for the community. Mystical and paradoxical, the hall features many sculptural elements such as the muses surrounding the stage, Wagner’s Valkyries emerging from the ceiling, and busts of Anselm Clavé and Ludwig van Beethoven. Decorative motifs of flowers, palm trees and fruit complete this unique space.
